title: Japan Club Sand Volleyball Social
summary: Meet prospective and returning Japan Club members through casual sand volleyball. Participants must sign the required RecSports waiver before playing.

title: Spikeball For A Cure
summary: Teams of two compete in a charity spikeball tournament. Entry requires creating and sharing a fundraising page benefiting the Andrew McDonough B+ Foundation.
hostOrganization: B+ at Notre Dame; Spikeball Roundnet Club

title: Flaherty 5K and 1 Mile Fun Color Run
summary: A colorful run and walk supports breast cancer research, with refreshments afterward. The listing welcomes participants of all ages; check it for sign-up details.

title: Grad Student Indoor Volleyball
summary: Graduate students meet for indoor volleyball in Rockne Memorial Gym. No experience is required.

title: GreeNDot Undergraduate Student Training
summary: A 2.5-hour undergraduate bystander certification training addresses interpersonal violence prevention. Check the original listing for registration requirements.

title: Graduate Research Ethics Workshop
summary: Graduate researchers discuss ethical research practices, mentoring, documentation, and AI with Dr. Allan Loup. The listing says this workshop counts toward the Graduate School ethics requirement.
hostOrganization: Graduate Student Government; Graduate School Ethics Office

title: Sophomore Showdown
summary: Sophomores unwind with free Spikeball, sand volleyball, cornhole, and other yard games. No skills are required; snacks and water are planned.

title: Senior Class Fall Dessert Social
summary: Seniors can stop by for free fall-themed desserts and connect with other members of their class.
location: Lobby Table A, Door 16 (see listing for building details)

title: JCC's Dunkin' and Pumpkins!
summary: Juniors gather on Library Lawn for Dunkin' Donuts and pumpkin painting to celebrate fall.

title: Wall Street Club Mentorship Event
summary: Upperclassmen and underclassmen with similar interests connect for support navigating Notre Dame's financial landscape. Check the listing for club participation requirements.

title: October Community Garden Workday
summary: Meet fellow gardeners, help with communal tasks, and tend plots at the Notre Dame Community Garden. Check the source for participation details.

title: Craft and Unwind: Student Concerns Drop-In
summary: A graduate student drop-in offers crafting, conversation about student life, supplies, and light refreshments.
location: Graduate Student Lounge (see source for directions)

title: Graduate Pumpkin Painting Workshop
summary: All graduate students are invited to a lightly guided pumpkin painting session. No painting experience is needed.

title: AAA Asian Allure Showcase
summary: The Asian American Association presents its annual cultural showcase with dancing, singing, and performances. Check the listing for admission details.
hostOrganization: Asian American Association of Notre Dame

title: Sprint Hack @ND — Sunday
summary: Companies bring real problems to this reverse-pitch hackathon, and teams demo solutions to venture and industry judges. Open attendance, any major, with meals covered; bring a team or form one on site.

title: SAI-Spark: AI Research Tutorial and Community
summary: A hands-on scientific AI tutorial welcomes graduate students, postdocs, and faculty across disciplines, with opportunities to connect with the SAI research community.

title: SAI-Spark: AI Research Tutorial and Community
summary: A standalone scientific AI tutorial for graduate students, postdocs, and faculty offers practical AI techniques and connections with the SAI community.

title: SAI-Spark: AI Research Tutorial and Community
summary: Graduate students, postdocs, and faculty explore scientific AI tools in a standalone tutorial and connect with researchers across disciplines.

title: Tech & Entrepreneurship 101
summary: Beyond the Dome introduces Arts & Letters students to careers in tech, startups, internships, and using the Notre Dame network. Registration is linked in the original listing.
hostOrganization: Beyond the Dome, College of Arts and Letters

title: Friday Pitches: Meet the IDEA Center and Investors
summary: Aspiring entrepreneurs pitch to the IDEA Center and investors for feedback and a chance at funding. Any student may watch; pitching requires an idea submission and startup-coach preparation.

title: Somos ND: Cafecito con Conciencia
summary: Students, staff, and faculty gather for meaningful conversations during Hispanic Heritage Month. Coffee and light refreshments are provided, and all are welcome.

title: Indiana CTSI Summit: Mental Health Research and Partnerships
summary: A research summit includes talks, posters, breakout sessions, and a networking lunch with topic tables. Registration closes October 7 at 5 p.m. Eastern. The agenda begins with breakfast at 7:30 a.m.; closing remarks begin at 3:45 p.m., with no finish time stated.
location: Morris Inn, Smith Ballroom and breakout rooms
hostOrganization: Indiana CTSI; Notre Dame Community Health and Clinical Partnerships

title: Materials Science and Engineering PhD Office Hours
summary: Program staff answer questions from current MSE PhD students and Notre Dame students interested in the program. No appointment is necessary for the in-person visit.
hostOrganization: Materials Science and Engineering PhD Program

title: Fall Undergraduate Research Fair
summary: Undergraduates discover research opportunities through speakers, posters, and institutional representatives. The deadline to register as a poster presenter is October 5.

title: Flu Vaccine Blitz — Tuesday
summary: On-campus flu vaccinations are open to students and specified Notre Dame medical-plan participants. Appointments are required; see the listing for eligibility and registration.

title: Flu Vaccine Blitz — Wednesday
summary: The second on-campus flu vaccination day welcomes students and specified Notre Dame medical-plan participants. Appointments are required; check eligibility and registration in the source.

title: The Solar Revolution: Photovoltaics and Our Energy System
summary: Qcells global CTO Danielle Merfeld discusses advances in solar technology, domestic manufacturing, energy storage, and space applications.

title: Campus Green Tour
summary: A public walking tour explores Notre Dame's sustainability initiatives. Only 20 spots are available; registration is required, and the tour is weather permitting.
location: Meet on the east side of Walsh Family Hall of Architecture

title: Football Fr(AI)days: Touchdowns in Science with AI
summary: Brett Savoie moderates a panel of campus experts about how AI accelerates discovery in science and engineering.
hostOrganization: Scientific AI Initiative; Data, AI, and Computing Initiative

title: The Science of How the Arts Save Lives: Daisy Fancourt
summary: Researcher and author Daisy Fancourt discusses how music, visual art, dance, theater, and museum experiences can support health and well-being.

title: Art on the Aux with DJ PB
summary: DJ PB creates a soundtrack for a museum visit, pairing rhythm and melody with the works of art on view.

title: AI Leaders of Tomorrow: Projects Showcase and Networking
summary: Students present applied AI projects developed with regional companies. A poster session and networking reception begin at 3:15 p.m. during the 2–4 p.m. showcase.
hostOrganization: iNDustry Labs; Data, AI, and Computing Initiative

title: HalloweenFest
summary: Student Activities lists HalloweenFest across Library Lawn, Duncan Patio, and Legends. Additional program details have not yet been published; check the source before attending.
location: Library Lawn, Duncan Patio, and Legends

title: Vibe Coding 101: Build an AI-Assisted Web Tool
summary: A hands-on workshop teaches browser-based conversational programming and publishing a simple web tool. No coding experience is needed; register through the linked library workshop calendar.
hostOrganization: AI Collaborative Programming: Hesburgh Libraries, ND Learning, and OIT
